title_en: Official Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Approving the Shandong High People's Court's Implementation of the Reform of Centralized Jurisdiction over Administrative Cases
keywords_en: administrative litigation; administrative case handling by High People's Court
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Reply on Approving the Shandong High People's Court to Carry Out Reform of Centralized Jurisdiction over Administrative Cases

Fa [2019] No. 156

Shandong High People's Court:

We have received your Request for Instructions on the Pilot Reform of Cross-Administrative-Region Jurisdiction over Administrative Cases by the Two-Level Courts of the Jinan Railway Transport Courts (Lu Gao Fa [2019] No. 5). Upon study, in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph 2 of Article 18 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and the spirit of the Guiding Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Centralized Jurisdiction over Administrative Cases by People's Courts across Administrative Regions (Fa Fa [2015] No. 8), we approve in principle your request.

The reform shall be promoted under the unified leadership and coordination of the local Party committee, in accordance with the spirit of the central institutional reform and the requirements of the institutional reform of this region. When detailing and implementing the reform plan, the administrative adjudication functions of the basic-level people's courts in various localities shall be retained, so as to maintain the integrity of the litigation system and serve local law-based administration. The intermediate people's courts may select one or two basic-level people's courts with a large number of cases, strong adjudication capability, good judicial environment, and convenient transportation as central courts to exercise centralized jurisdiction. The plaintiff's right of choice shall be fully respected; the plaintiff may choose either the court of the defendant's place or the central court to have jurisdiction. Local courts and centralized jurisdiction courts shall strengthen communication and connection, coordinate the separation and combination of mediation and adjudication, and jointly work on the coordination and resolution of administrative disputes. If railway courts are to be used for centralized jurisdiction over some administrative cases, specific issues such as the transfer of key administrative adjudication personnel must be handled first to avoid a decline in the quality of administrative adjudication, and the future direction of railway court reform and centralized jurisdiction over other types of cases should also be considered. A mechanism for unifying adjudication standards shall be established to prevent inconsistencies in the standards for similar cases due to different courts of jurisdiction. Before the implementation of the Plan, an announcement shall be made to the public. Your court shall strengthen research and guidance, and promptly report any new situations and problems arising in the implementation to the Supreme People's Court.
